utterances.text: Yes, the friendly soldier who was really friendly to us, he pushed her away and he says, move, move, so we had to move quickly through Savici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did you in fact -- you and your family went to Garici but did some of the other people with you stay in a place called Vakufci?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That is correct, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you remain in Garici?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I'll say approximately 30 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And then again, because of the problem with food, did you and your mother go to Bilice?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That is correct, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And whilst you were in Bilice, did your brother arrive?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when he arrived, what did he want you to do?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: He told us that Bilice will no longer stay under control of Croats and that we should go to Vecici with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you go at that stage to Vecici?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: No, ma'am. We went back to Garici again because we were afraid to go to -- to pass to Kotor Varos and passing Vrbanja which was most -- Vrbanja had mines so we were afraid to go back so we went back to Garici again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear what happened to Bilice?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was that?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Most of the people and soldiers who were there, they surrendered and they were offered if they surrendered they going to live and they going to be transferred to Bosnian side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you had gone back to Garici again. Roughly how long did you remain there?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Say 25 to 30 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. By this stage - I think we've come roughly into October or thereabouts - were there any villages outside of Garici and Vecici which were not under Serb control?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Vecici was the only village left under control of people defended themselves from Serbs. Everything else was under control of Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you then eventually, some four days before Vecici fell, go there?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That is correct, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you do that as a result of, effectively, orders?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I remember one night we were sitting at Atif Agambegovic who was my relative and we were sitting there watching the news when somebody knocked on the door and at that moment, we opened the door and Akif Pasic which was my next door neighbour and also cousin arrived and told us that they signed a truce or agreement with the Serbs that there would be no fighting for five days and that all the people, all the civilians from Hrvacani should go to Vecici. That was the agreement with the Serbs. And next morning we left for Vecici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you had to go via Vrbanjci to pick up a travel document; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, roughly how many of you went to Vecici that day?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I'll say approximately 30 to 50 people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, was that women and children?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That is correct, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived at Vecici, what sort of state was the town in? Or the village?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: When we were approaching Vecici from Vrbanjci, most of the houses, I mean all of them, were destroyed. We met some soldiers waiting for us and they had trees all over the road so we had a hard time to get in Vecici, but all the houses were burned and most of them, I would say 100 per cent destroyed because of shelling and all the stuff that was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you hear that the village had been aerially bombarded?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you also meet in Vecici your father and your brother?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was your brother-in-law there as well?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That is correct, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that stage, did you know what had happened to your sister?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: She had been living, you've told us, in Dabovci. What had happened to that village?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Dabovci was -- I don't know what happened. I -- how they got -- we heard from him when we came to Vecici that the whole village was destroyed, burned, and all the civilians were taken to Vrbanjci and all the men were gathered together, including himself, and they were shot, but he -- he has survived, and then he escaped to Vecici. All the houses were burned and the civilians were taken to Vrbanjci, including my sister.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your sister at Vecici?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: No, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to jump ahead for a moment. When was the first time you saw your sister again?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: When we came to safe side, Travnik and Zenica, when she came to visit us from Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'll come back to that later. I want you to have a look, now, please, at a video --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, which there is a transcript for. I'm not -- it's a very long video and I'm only going to play parts of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Does this item have a number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This is -- I'm sure it has because this is a video which contains a lot of other material.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's not an exhibit yet, Your Honour, although it's got -- can we pause it for a moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have referred to it in the past already, no?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, although it contains the same news reel at the end that we've seen on other videos, it's a different one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Its number is V 000-2908 and it will become Exhibit 2431. If we could play it? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We seem to have lost the sound, though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The transcript itself will have what number?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could we call that 2431-1?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: A and B because there is a B/C/S version as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But I don't know why the sound is not coming up. Maybe it's just because I haven't got the ear phones on.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: I now have a picture of Ms. Korner, I don't know if for some reason I'm not using this correctly. I pressed the video button.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you not have a Sanction machine over there? It's on computer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You go on computer evidence and tell me if there is a problem, Madam Baruch.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm still wondering why there is no sound.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: I'm just seeing, Your Honours, grey and white. Okay. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We still have no sound.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, we don't have any sound. Well, Your Honour, this is on a CD-ROM but I have actually got a video here so we could give that to the video booth to play it. Can we pause just there, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We just caught sight there of a grave stone saying, a headstone I should say, saying Ekrem Pasic. Was that any relation to you, Mr. Pasic?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A close relation?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: He was my cousin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know how he died? Did you hear how he died?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes. When we got to Vecici, his father told us that Ekrem Pasic and his friend, I don't recall his name, I don't remember his name, left for Travnik and they were shot above Vecici north side, small village, I remember now name, Staza, also controlled by Serbs. They left at night and they -- the people at front lane heard a lot of fighting going on and like four days later his father went over there and he found his body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. If we can continue playing the video, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We seem to have lost the sound again. The sound is gone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The sound is gone or it never came actually.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Somebody said it did come. We can give them the video to play, Your Honour, that might be easier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Ms. Korner, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: At this point if it's being played as a video then I press the video button?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think so, yes. Although you might find it clearer sometimes if you press video evidence. It depends. Sometimes it's --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If we can play it, then, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Still tracking. Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] Soldiers from all the villages are here. We can't go from one grave to the next, but we'll just go over so that you can see. Tell them that the whole family is here, a whole family, father, child and wife. A shell killed them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could we pause the video there, please? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That appears to be some kind of the remains of a shelf some kind. Did you see that yourself, Mr. Pasic?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who showed it to you?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: My father.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, could we just carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, so where are we, here, now?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm so sorry, we are in Vecici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Pasic, can you just confirm that is Vecici?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes, there is when I moved to Vecici my father showed me this shell from air strikes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour is quite right. I forgot to say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed, yeah.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] What you see up there are napalm bombs; they threw them too. And who did that? Our Serbian neighbours, our kums, and perhaps the last name, Zoran Zajdan [phoen], Zoran, our neighbours did that. Who else? This is a newly-built mosque. It was to be opened on the 1st of August, but you see what happened to it, due to the situation here, our situation -- our neighbours did it. Over 200 missiles of all kinds and calibres were fired from tanks, guns, howitzers and what else, not to mention the bullets. They shelled from all sides, you see. Knocked the minaret down. Some 2 million marks were invested in it. Neighbours -- our -- the neighbours are destroying everything they come across, shelling daily, although there is nothing left of it. They have destroyed it completely. This is the state of the mosque on the inside. This was one of the best preserved mosques in this region. You can see what's left of it now. There is a piece of shrapnel here inside. There are pieces of shells here, some armour-piercing ones over there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we pause, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: I don't know if -- I think this video has not been shown before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: So I think that the testimony that's coming through, along with the video, is unsworn testimony that hasn't been offered as a 92 bis motion and I would object to further sound on this video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is the first time I've heard this objection. We've watched video after video after video with the sound. Your Honours are entitled to take into consideration and give it the weight that it deserves, given as, quite rightly, Ms. Baruch says it's not sworn testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not being taken as sworn testimony anyway. But I still don't understand the objection as such. I mean we have had videos where we did not listen to the sound, precisely because we decided not to listen to the sound.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I put it this way --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But obviously this is not the case. We listen and then obviously if you want to pause at any time and put a question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm going to in a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sorry. You do that. Say, is this the mosque in Vecici, and he would say yes, but it's his testimony that I would -- we would take into consideration as such, together with the video but I understand in a way what you mean but you don't need to worry about it, Madam Baruch.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: What I'm understanding the Court say something you will consider what you see and this witness's testimony, but not what you're hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What we are hearing may become important if questions are put. For example, if the commentary, running commentary says there is napalm here et cetera, no questions are put on whether -- for me it doesn't mean a thing. I mean at that point --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour I agree entirely it's hearsay testimony and it's hearsay testimony in exactly the same way as Your Honours take into consideration other hearsay testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But you don't need to worry about it unduly, Mrs. Baruch, because basically it's being shown to the witness and he will be asked questions if and when, and it's his questions that are the important part.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Okay. With that understanding I just have made my objection for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's all right. Thanks. Okay. So, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: While we've paused the film for a moment --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic did you yourself see the destruction to this mosque?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is the newest -- the interpreter said it earlier, there is a new mosque and I was walking by with my father.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you go inside it?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: No, I did not because I was afraid it, you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Maybe booby trapped or something probably.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't think it was booby trapped at that stage, but all right. Can we just continue very shortly then I'm going to ask for the film to be moved on slightly. Can you just continue playing on at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Actually, we saw two persons walking at one time. Did you feature in this video yourself or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, later we'll see a date on it. It was the 3rd of October, it was filmed, before Mr. Pasic got there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I think we'll move on. Can we fast-forward, I hope the timing is the same, to roughly 13 minutes, please, on this? Your Honour, I'm going to the part on page 3 of the transcript, that voice at line 20, where it says, "Voice." At least I hope I am.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: I don't have a transcript. Does the Court have a transcript?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It was given to you last Friday. Can we stop the film, sorry and go back?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is the transcript which has as ERN on the first page 0308-3027.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Pause now, please, the film.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Again, I still have my objection to the words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we'll see this gentleman come into focus, could we just move it at a normal rate, please. The film. Play on. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, pause, please, there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Pasic, do you recognise this man?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who is he?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: He's hodza from Vecici. I saw him when I was at Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you seen -- did you see him during the short period you were in Vecici or was the first time at Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: First time was at Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Yes. I think if we just run through this part, then, please? And then we'll stop. Yes, could you play that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] Let me just film the building a bit or what remains of it so you can see for yourself what and how it happened and it could have been avoided. A man who is trying to be a better person is happy in both worlds and a man who -- he can talk now. A person who works for the general good is happy in both worlds and if people were like that, luck would follow us for as long as we live and we would not blame ourselves, nor would either blame us. Do we want to be like this? We should be like this. If we want to keep our own happiness, peace, and freedom, we must be like this, because they say that one man has a duty to look after another and respect him like he does himself, and there is no faith or any neighbourly behaviour for those who do not live with their neighbours in the best way. Efendi, tell us who is to blame for all of this so that all our fathers, brothers, relatives, colleagues and friends and our neighbours will know when they watch this tape, who is to blame for everything that is happening here? Not only in our village but in all of Bosnia-Herzegovina? Whose fault is it? Is it us Muslims or -- I just ask myself this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I can tell you straight and plain.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Pause for a minute. Your Honour is going to hear evidence that this man is dead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But what I mean to say, if this part of his contribution to the video, to the commentary --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're not going to rely that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm not going to rely on what he says but I think Your Honour ought to hear what this man has to say because you're going to hear about the circumstances in which this man died.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: M'hm.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, could we just finish this off, please?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] He who does not attack, he's happy to remain at peace, and everyone will be peaceful because of him. And he who attacks is the one who is an aggressor against himself and others. I think it makes sense. I would really like everyone to be -- it is not a matter of what direction or what faith or religion they are. I would like all of us to be honest and trust each other. God demands it of us but so does man, the one who cares for the well-being of man. Efendi, one more question, have you been here since the very first day? Yes. Since when? From the first day you have not gone anywhere or been out of this house here. No, since the very first day I was the one who started building it with my people here, and we built it, and then I moved into it. As far as my Dzematlija [phoen] congregation is concerned, they were always willing to get on with everyone and all the other neighbours, regardless of their denomination, know that. There are 18 denominations in our state, our former joint collective state, they were 18 religious denominations and in Bosnia-Herzegovina alone, there were 16 different ones. If you consider this statement, then Bosnia-Herzegovina is the symbol of happiness and well-being of all people regardless of their nature, because we have many denominations here, 16, in fact, and there were two denominations in the other republics. One more thing: Would you like to send greetings to anyone because this will be shown in Austria, Germany, Switzerland, in the whole world, the whole world will watch this video so if you have anyone you would like to say hello to, Efendi? To all our people there, to our Muslims, I send greetings and to all Catholics and all others who are good-natured and who wish to live a good life with us, to all, I send greetings, so they would be joyful and happy, happy about the greeting, because it comes from the heart. What else can I say? That's all from Efendi, and I wish that God gives you all the best everywhere and that you have luck in everything. Not just you but all of those who are your friends and that those who are against man move away from evil and follow the path that is needed for the good of man. Thank you. May you live long.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. You can stop the video, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Pasic, you spent I think some four days in Vecici; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That is correct, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened on the fifth day?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: On the fifth day, I was on the east side in Vecici and we were sitting in the basement when my father came and he was talking to my mom about me going with him for Travnik, because he heard and they were afraid to send me with my mom because Serbs were taking kids and all the males from females in Banja Luka and Vlasic. So they got afraid and they decided that I go with my father and we left that night around, I'd say, approximately 8.00 at night, a group of people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, before you left, had there been any attack going on, on Vecici?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: No major attacks, just sporadic automatic weapons, snipers, but no, no major fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you left at about 9.00 that night, a group of you. How big was the group?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how many people but it was long, a long group. I know for a fact. I don't know exactly how many people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that include your father?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes, including my father.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about your brother?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: No, my brother, I guess he left a day before or, I don't know where he -- what time he left or when, but -- later on, we found him in Travnik so I guess he escaped the day before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about however your brother-in-law? Was he part of the group?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was part of the group. As a matter of fact we were holding hands when we were walking. My father was in the front, I was behind him, I was holding my uncle and, you know, we were trying to stay closer together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your brother-in-law, you couldn't remember what the family name was, what was his first name do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: His first name, Elvir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, of this group?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I remember last name now, Lihovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of this group, what proportion were women and children?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Can you explain that? I mean --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you have said there a was a group of people and you can't remember how many. But roughly how many women, your mother was there, you told us, were there other women and roughly how many?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Well, all the villagers from Vecici and mainly villagers from Hrvacani, they left behind in Vecici, I don't know how many, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there a number of children, people your age, in your group?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: In my group, yes. As a matter of fact, two of them were going in -- were going in the same school and they were my age.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And how did you leave? Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: As I mentioned before, we left around 8.00, 9.00 and we were going towards Travnik and we were just walking with -- all night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did that take you through open country or woods?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Woods.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened the next -- what happened during that night, rather?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Around midnight, I'd say 1.00 or 2.00 in the morning, we were ambushed by Serbs. I don't know exactly where but I know it was just woods, you know, and lots of forest, so we were ambushed and two people got killed, a guy from Vecici and his son, last name Zec and I don't remember his name but I saw them and we took them and left them behind, underneath a tree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the group remain as one at that stage? In other words did everybody stay together or did they split?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: No, we split in two groups and then later on that night, around I'd say 4.00, 5.00 in the morning, we found each other, both groups, and we gathered together to rest in one open area which was surrounded by woods.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you discovered there?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I assume all night, later on we found out that we had somebody that was talking to the Serbs in our group, but that night, or I'd say morning, they knew where we were going exactly, what position, and what stage, so around early morning, they were waiting for us to rest or gather together to -- and then that's the moment when we were ambushed the second time, early in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to your group?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Well, fighting started and bullets were coming from everywhere. I was so terrified and so scared that we ran, one group ran with our leader, Besim, who was leading the group. We ran down the hill into the water. I don't know the name of the hill or neither the water name. We ran down and some of the fighters -- other group decided to fight Serbs so they fighting was going on up on the hill. We ran down and we land on -- most of our groups -- front land on the mines. They knew exactly which way we were going so they had mine fields near the water and thank God I was stopped. I had a big, big, huge -- I mean, coat on me, and it was so wet that I stopped my father and I told him to take it off, and by that time, people passed us and they land on the mines. Including Besim, who was leader, his two legs were blown up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You managed to avoid going into the mine field. Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: We went around the water and -- actually we passed through the water, which two men went and they told us that no mines were found so we crossed the river on the other side where we gathered, I'd say, 200, 150 to 200 people including hodza and we gathered together and we prayed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: And at that time, fighting was still going on and Serbs on both hills, they were calling our names, "Balija, surrender, there is no way you can go. Just give up your weapons and you'll be free." And they were calling on megaphones, names, and we just didn't know what to do. I was so scared that I didn't know what to do, where to go, so we were just sitting there and prayed and finally we decided to surrender.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you surrendered, how did you indicate that you were surrendering?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: First of all, we walk into the old tunnel with 200 people, and the guy who was contacting Serbs all the time, he pulled his shirt, took his shirt off, which was white shirt, and he raised it on the stick, and that's when Serbs told us to walk slowly towards them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that what you did?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That is correct. We walked slowly towards Serbs. They were waiting for us. I'd say approximately a hundred or 200 metres from the tunnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your father and your brother-in-law, Elvir, in the group with you?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened when you got to where the Serbs were?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Okay. When we got to the Serbs, there were -- they were firing weapons and all around us, they told us to -- if anybody who had a weapon to lay weapon on one side, all the money and gold on the other side, and they told us if they find a needle they would kill us. So nothing, just empty all our pockets and walk slowly towards this -- right before Grabovica school, so I don't know what the place and field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you got to the field, what happened to the men? And yourselves?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Okay. When we got there, soldiers told us to lay down in I'd say three rows like this. We were faced this way down to the ground, and the ground was so muddy and wet that we had a hard time to breathe. They told us to lay down and just stay calm. If anybody moves they are going to shoot us. And we were there approximately two hours face down and that's when the all the things started happening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what started happening?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: First of all, they asked us who was in charge, and they picked a guy from the group, I don't know his name or anything because I couldn't see because I was face down, they picked a guy and asked him who was in charge and he says, Besim. And they asked him where he is at, and he said, he got shot, he's wounded and probably dead right now. And they told him to call his name so he started yelling his name and they were laughing and, you know, firing guns and he came back to his group, he lay down, and that's when they start asking questions who had this gun. As a matter of fact they had a list of guns and they called the names, so they called my father, I don't know for what reason, but he was next to me and they told him to get up and they had a number of his gun because he was a hunter, he had a licence for it and they were saying, where did you find those boots? He told them I was a hunter, and they said, no, no, that's not true. You killed one of our soldiers and they start beating him. So he was crying and they asked him also, do you have any members within the group? And he told them no. But he did came back to the group. They were also beating the hodza. I know they called his name and they were screaming and laughing, he says this guy is in charge. So he was beaten, he was crying and I know he was saying, no I'm not responsible for none of this, my child. That was his favourite saying, my child, and I don't know what happened to him but later on when I got up I saw him in blood and he was faced this way. I couldn't walk -- I couldn't turn around and see because they told us to look straight not to look around. And when we were laying down on the ground face down, they had three -- later on I found out three army trucks parked next to the group, and they were going back and forth, just to terrify us and see if somebody stands up and they told us if somebody gets up they are going to shoot us so they were going back and forth and my uncle told me they are going to run over us and they did -- they went back and they came forward but they didn't run over us. That was just to see if somebody is going to get up so they can shoot him. At that moment, they told us all the children and women to get up, I refused because I didn't know what's going to happen, what was going to happen, but my uncle said, you going to survive, go. So I finally got up and I walked away with the group of I'd say six boys my age and women and one injured guy. So they told us to walk towards Grabovica which we were -- we did. We walked down and they -- I don't know what happened to the men. They left later on, when we got to Grabovica school, they lined us in line and that's -- it was kind of dark, I couldn't see, a guy, but I guess he was in charge of the group, he approached us and he told us to -- he was kind of -- he said that nothing is going to happen to us, tomorrow they are going to have a bus for us to go to Travnik but he did say our fighters will pay for this and then he told us to walk in the school and they are going to put us in the classroom and that's what they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pause for a moment there. When you got to the school, in the village of Grabovica, were there local Serbs there?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes. Women and children, they were dressed, mostly women, were dressed in black dress, they were screaming and throwing stones and spitting on us and they were waiting for us even though it was kind of dark at night they were waiting outside and yelling, but the soldiers got us through and we walked in the school and we were put in a classroom on the first floor. Then later on that night, we saw all the men, the rest of the men, coming with their hands tied up behind their back. They were put on the second floor, all of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the person in charge of the group who said that nothing was going to happen to you, that you would be taken to Travnik, and that, was he wearing any kind of a uniform?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Like I said, it was kind of dark, I know he had some kind of hat or something with lights and I couldn't see him. He was a tall man. And he had camouflage uniforms but I couldn't see any marks or anything because it was too dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you were put into the ground floor in a classroom. Were you being guarded? I'm so sorry, you were put in a classroom on the first floor. Just so that we get this right, do you mean by that the ground floor or actually going up some stairs?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Well, actually, they didn't have ground floor. It was just one, I don't know, no basement at all, so yes it was --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you went?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Straight in the classroom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you came through the door you were taken into a classroom?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you saw the men come in you say they were placed on the second floor, so that was the floor above you?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes, they had steps going up so we heard them walking upstairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Was there a guard placed on you?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes, two men, two soldiers whom, one of them was a prisoner in Vecici, and he was really kind. He had an automatic weapon and he says -- he asked us later on that night, do you remember me? I was in Vecici. And we didn't -- we were afraid to talk but, yeah, two soldiers were guarding us that night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say that when the men arrived, they had their hands tied up behind their back. Did you see that yourself or did somebody else see that from a window?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I see it myself -- I saw it myself because they had -- they had trucks with lights, it was raining, I remember it was raining that night, it was so dark, and they had trucks behind with the lights in front of them so we could see them walking in a group. I was looking through the window. They were on our left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, whilst you were being kept at the school and after the fighters arrived, were you given the -- the men arrived, were you given any opportunity to go and see them?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes. They offered us later on that night, I don't know exactly, at one time, if we wanted to see our relative or whoever in that group. I refused that. I didn't want to go because I was afraid, and at that time, you know, I knew my father, when they told him before to get up and they were asking him about the boots, and they also asked him about members, any members within the group and he told them no so that's why I didn't want to go and see him because I was afraid to go but some other people from our group went to see their relatives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your mother go and speak to your father?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you kept in the classroom all night?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that some people from the group went to see their relatives. When they came back, did they tell you the condition of the men who were up there?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Harija Ahmedovic [phoen] is the name of one lady who was on my right hand side sitting and she wanted to see her husband because she just recently got married. She went upstairs and his name was Sead Rahmanovic, he was from Okuci [phoen]. And she said -- she went upstairs and she talked to them and she -- when she came downstairs she said that they were all fine, you know, they were all upstairs, all of them, but they were beaten and as a matter of fact her husband, she said he had a black eye and his face was all blue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, what happened the next morning?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Next morning, two soldiers, I mean, came to us and told us that we were going for Travnik, they have a bus ready for us, and they told us walk slowly from the classroom and as we were walking out, a bunch of people, civilians, mostly women and children, were waiting for us outside school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened as you came out of the school?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: As we came -- as we came out of the school, they told us to walk one by one, slowly, and they had people on both sides, it was like a tunnel, we had to walk and a bus was parked approximately 50 to 100 metres from the school, and I remember the soldier told us if you survive this, you're going to survive, and the people waiting outside, they were holding axes, sticks, stones, they were just waiting for us to walk through the group so -- and they -- the first man who I remember was going to school with me, a little boy, they let him through, and as soon as he meet the middle of the group they hit him so hard with I don't know what but he fell down on his knees and he couldn't walk so he crawled, and when the second man was passing by he grabbed him and took him to the bus so we had to go one by one and walk slowly. We couldn't run because they told us walk slowly so they can beat us and I was the last person in the group. They let me go and I was beaten on my back and as soon as I reached the bus, one woman grabbed me, was dressed in a black dress, and told, let me kill this little balija because my two sons died in Vecici, and she was holding a knife, and I didn't move. I didn't know what to do. I was so scared. And thank God that the soldier grabbed her and pushed her away and told me, get in there. He pushed me in the bus and they closed the door, and the bus was -- I assume they had some problems so we didn't leave that spot until 15 minutes later, because they had some problems. While we were waiting on the bus, people were so angry, they were throwing stones and spitting on us. They told us not to look around we might get hurt if we looked through the window, we might get hurt. But I did. I looked through the window when we left that spot, and I saw some people from upstairs where our men were located, they waved like this and that was the last time I saw men from Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever since that day seen your father or your brother-in-law again?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: No, ma'am, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want you to look, please, just at one document, which is Exhibit P2302. Now, if you can -- I think you can put the English on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Put it straight on the ELMO, and then we can follow too because I don't have this document right in front of me now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we look, please, at item number 2, the paragraph: "In the area of Kotor Varos, there was a clash between members of Muslim forces and our units, because of the refusal to negotiate on moving out of the Vecici village area. About 40 Green Beret members were killed and about 200 were captured. A brutal massacre of the captured members of the Green Berets started because of the wounding of four and killing of one soldier of the Kotor Varos Light Infantry Brigade and the burning of wounded soldiers on the Gola Planina, Jajce." Is there any doubt in your mind, Mr. Pasic, that that refers to the men who you left behind in the school at Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: No doubt in my mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once you had left in the buses, did you go to Vrbanjci?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from there, did you go to Travnik?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes. With 13 other buses, including all civilians, all women and children from Vecici and some surrounding villages, they were waiting for us to arrive from Grabovica and we were taken with the buses, 13 other buses, towards Travnik, across Vlasic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anything happen before you got to Travnik?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the Vlasic we were stopped with a group of soldiers, four of them, four groups, within like 15 metres, they were all armed, they had masks on their faces and they were like every 15 metres that we were stopped and asked for all the money, gold, anything, to leave, and so they were actually stripping all of us to find the gold and money.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And once they had taken everything off you, how did you get to Travnik?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina knew about this and they were waiting for us, I don't know how far from the lines, but they were waiting for us with the buses and we had to walk, I don't know how big was the distance, but finally we met Bosnian army and they took us with trucks and buses towards Travnik and Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to go, please, Your Honour for a moment into private session, if I may?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's go into private session, Madam Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, what effect did all of what happened to you and your family have on you personally?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: This incident that happened left a deep impact in my life. I still have nightmares. As a matter of fact, last night I dreamt about my father. Every time when I go back and I think about this, it just brings the memories and it's really hard.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Korner. I think if you agree, we should have the break now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 25 minutes. And then they will cross-examine the witness. So basically, we'll say we'll reconvene at quarter to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who is witness 7.279? This is yours, Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's tomorrow's witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know him by BT, all right. It's all right. I got confused.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I always forget what the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, it's my fault, it's my fault, it's my fault.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's the list for tomorrow's witness, BT95.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because I really had a fright. For a moment I thought this was the cross-examination documents for this witness. And I said I hope not. All right, Mrs. Baruch is going to cross-examine you. I think I ought to explain to you that this is part of the procedure. The accused is entitled here to have you cross-examined on the basis of your testimony. So it's something that we need to go through and Mrs. Baruch, who represents the accused, is one of the lawyers representing the accused, will be conducting the cross-examination. Mrs. Baruch?

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Thank you, may it please the Court. Your Honours, just very briefly could we have it closed because it was closed for a small portion of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Closed or private?

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session for a while.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Pasic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. We are in open session now. Yes, Mrs. Baruch.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was two points I wanted to clear up, I think the Court suggested that your fear of going into the mosque, that was on videotape, might have been because it was booby-trapped. But did I understand correctly that that mosque was in Vecici and under the control of Muslims and Croat forces?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That is correct, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the Serbs would have had nothing to do with booby-trapping that mosque at that time? Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: The only reason why I was afraid to walk in the mosque, because of all the shelling and all the bombing, I was afraid that the mosque could collapse. That's why we don't -- I was standing next to it and I was just, you know, examine it around in it but we didn't me and my father -- I didn't -- I refused to walk in there because I was afraid that the building would collapse and -- because of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know if -- was that mosque quite close to the area where there was fighting?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Well, this is -- the newest mosque was --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The one we saw the picture of.

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't tell you that. I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Vecici a very large place or is it a smaller place?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: It's a big -- well, it's quite a big village. I don't know how many houses or anybody but they had in Vecici they were split with the river. We had a west side and an east side with two mosques so...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the particular mosque we were talking about, do you remember if it was on the west side or the east side?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I think it was on the east side because that was the side we stayed in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We being you and your family?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes, my mom and I and my father.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you also talked about being stopped on your way to Travnik. Now, the bus that you were in, that bus, was it filled with the people that you had been in that school with? I think it's called Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Grabovica, yes, ma'am, as I mentioned before it was approximately 13 buses and the last bus was a bus filled with us from -- coming from Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And as I understood it, you said that everything had been taken out of your house so you had lost the possessions from your house and when you were going with the fighting men - about 200 people, you said, who were captured - the Serb soldiers who captured you had said, take everything out of your pockets, don't even have a toothpick, I think you said; right?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: A needle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A needle, okay. And so at that point, when you were on the bus to Travnik, you had no possessions at that time, did you?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I think somebody asked if your mother -- I think Ms. Korner asked if your mother had gone upstairs to visit your dad when you were in the classroom in Grabovica, and I had understood that you were separated from your mother and your mother never got to that school because your mother went with the women and most of the children to Travnik immediately from where the fighting had been; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That is correct. I was kind of surprised, too, because, as I mentioned before, I left that night with my father and my mom stayed in Vecici, which later on she left with all the civilians that morning when we arrived I saw her in the bus with the rest of my family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: She wasn't in Grabovica with me, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you talked about when your -- I think it was your uncle, maybe it was your cousin, had come to get you to bring you to Vecici. Was it your uncle or your cousin?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: No. That was my brother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, your brother?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yeah. Actually I'll take that back. When I was in Garici my cousin Akif Pasic he came, yeah, he came with two soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He came with two Serb soldiers, right?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they had made a truce and an agreement; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your understanding was that if the people from your village, which was Hrvacani, would return to Vecici, then the -- if the fighting men surrendered there, that they would be safe and they would be exchanged over to the other side; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: No, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you want to think about that or did you want to --

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I just -- I don't understand. Can you repeat that question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. I think you need to rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And place it in a specific point in time. Because I think that's what's confusing the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Okay. For everybody, I'm looking at around page 7 of his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So read from his statement straight away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The part of it I got wrong. When you -- it says we stayed at Garici for a long time in the house of my cousin Atif by this time all the villages in the area except for Vecici had fallen to Serbs four days before --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Four days before Vecici fell we were sitting in Atif's house when another cousin of ours, Akif, came. He was armed and looked terrible. He had a beard and long hair and was untidy and there were two armed soldiers with him who were waiting outside the house for him. He informed us that we made an agreement with the Serbs that all refugees from Hrvacani had to go to Vecici. He informed us that the next morning, we had to go to Vrbanjci to get travel documents. That part is correct; right?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That is correct, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And some place -- I thought I saw that you had said, and I can't find it right now, that if the men at Vecici would then surrender at Vecici, they would be exchanged, is that --

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I never mentioned that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you don't have knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: No, I don't have knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Throughout your journeys from your village to the other villages that you went, there were Serb soldiers who helped you and the women and at times even protected you; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: One soldier, I don't know his name. That was one soldier when we came to Hrvacani. He was the kindest one in that particular group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But even when you left Vecici, when you were captured, there was a soldier who said, "I guarantee you're not going to get hurt." Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: But he -- he was -- I guess he was in charge but what he mentioned, he says, you -- what he meant -- I -- children and women, he kind of guaranteed that we are not going to get hurt but what he says, but your men, what he meant, father and rest of it, they will pay for this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. He was talking about the fighting men but with regard to the women and children, in the statement that I have, at least.

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says, I guarantee that nothing will happen to you. And that was for the women and the children?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who had accompanied the fighting men. So two times, two times, people at least -- Serb soldiers were looking out that you wouldn't get hurt or be killed?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yeah, but what happened that night, that was the night when we came to Grabovica but next morning we were beaten by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The women?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Local -- yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there were women there, you said they were Serb women, and I think when you said they were dressed in black --

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was how you knew or assumed they were all Serb women, right?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they had axes in their hands and they were beating you with wood but not with the axe head?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you had to walk through there, one woman grabbed you and she was distraught; wasn't she?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: She was crying and screaming and she said at that time that she lost two sons?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Vecici and so she wanted to take her revenge on you because of her loss; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that point, a Serb soldier grabbed you and threw you in the bus?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To keep her from being able to do anything, any harm to your body with a knife; right? Is that a yes?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That is correct, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you were at Vecici, before you went over to Grabovica, the Serb army separated the men fighters from the women and children because the women who stayed there, like your mother, they were going to go off to Travnik; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Can you repeat that, from Vecici to where?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you left Vecici --

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- the last time, you were going to that last town, Grabovica. And before you left for Grabovica with the fighting men, the Serb soldiers separated the men - the fighter people - from the women and children; didn't they?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I don't recall that, because we left Vecici and Serbs didn't know about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They didn't know that you had left?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: They didn't know but later on we found out that we had a man with us who cooperated with the Serbs, but no, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you separated yourself out, that is the fighting men separated themselves out and the women and children who were going to go off to Travnik, like your mother --

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- they stayed in Vecici?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the men, the fighting men, went through the woods, through the forest?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yeah, because we heard that convoys before us, the Serbs were taking all the male boys -- I mean all the males away from females in Banja Luka and also in Vlasic. That's why my father came to my mom and told her to go with him because he was afraid that if I go with my mom, I might get killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. He thought you might be mistaken for a fighting person?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That is correct, but --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So because of that fear, your father suggested that you not stay with the women and children, but that you go with him and with your brother and with your uncle as they made their escape; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Some women chose to go with them as well?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ten women, I think you said, that included two young girls?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And some boys of your age also accompanied the fighting men; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where they were going at that time? Were they trying to escape the Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: We were trying to go to -- for Travnik, definitely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So go on your own to Travnik not with the women who stayed behind?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. By a different route. And I think at one point in your statement, you said there were about 200 people who were walking with you through the woods and forest with the fighting men; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I mentioned 200 people, ready to surrender in the tunnel, we counted approximately 200 people when we were about to surrender.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: But I don't know what happened to the other group or other people because fighting was still going on on the other side of the river.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because some of the younger men decided to stop and make a stand and fight with the Serbs; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this Court would know that there were more than 200 people, including the fighting men, who left with you and your father when you left Vecici to go through the woods; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That's right. As I said before, it was a long line. I don't know how many people in the line when we left Vecici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And those people who you left with, although you didn't have a gun, many of the men who had been fighting in Vecici, many of those men were still armed and they took their guns with them; correct?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I'd say yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And in fact, you never counted the guns; did you?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you know that there were a lot of guns because -- for two reasons: One, one small group of young men decided to leave the bigger group and make a stand and fight off the Serbs, so they had weapons; correct?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when the Serbs finally captured you, after you came out of the tunnel, those Serbs said, hold up your weapons and then said, put the weapons on one side and the valuables on the other side, so you know that there were weapons, many weapons, with you at the time, as you were walking with those 200 people or hiding with the 200 people in that tunnel.

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I've seen some weapons but I don't know how many.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course. Now, you talked about people who were collaborating with the Serbs, some people who you noticed were on the radio. But I thought you also said that it was a collective decision of that group of 200 people who had tried to escape through the woods, it was a collective decision at that point to surrender to the Serbs. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That's right. In our group was a plan who was collaborating with Serbs. What I said, the way he was contacting Serbs, when we got ambushed the second time, we saw him standing -- he was behind a tree and he was talking on the radio with the Serbs. But later on, he was in our group, which -- he escaped with us, and as a matter of fact, when we went to Grabovica, one of the Serb soldiers came up to him and he says, nice job, and he left Grabovica with us for Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But despite this collaboration by that man, it was still a collective decision of the group in the tunnel to surrender at that point; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Is it correct, then, that your father and the men who left Vecici with you, they didn't want to surrender to the Serbs, that wasn't their intention when they left Vecici. It was their intention to escape not to surrender?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's true, because when Bilice got under control of Serbs, we heard that all the fighters, Croats and some Muslims, gave their weapons to the Serbs and they were beaten, they were taken to Banja Luka, and some other concentration camps or whatever, that's why a lot of people got afraid, that's why we escaped because we thought even though some of -- most of us didn't have weapons. We thought if they captured us -- because we were going to get killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just go back to that for a minute to make sure I understood it. There were some Muslims from Vecici who had been captured. Is that what you just said, and they had been brought to Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: No. What I said when Bilice which was a last stand in Croat standing in Kotor Varos before Vecici was under control, they finally gave up -- surrendered, they gave up the weapons and everything. They got promised, the Serbs promised them they going to be safe and they going to leave for Travnik, but also some soldiers or, I say, men from surrounding villages were in Bilice at that time and they left with Croat people, when Bilice got under control of Serbs. But no, I don't know about Vecici fighters or anybody that surrendered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So that's where the idea -- the misrecollection got in my head that there was an offer, if you surrender, we'll exchange you for other soldiers. That happened in Bilice where the Serbs said if you surrender, we will let you go to Travnik, or exchange you for other BiH prisoners; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I don't know about the exchanging but, yeah, they told people, fighters, if you surrender, you going to be -- which happened, most of them made it to Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: But they never said anything about Vecici surrendering and if you give up your weapon you're going to survive or anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But because -- it was because of the fear of the Muslim troops who were at Vecici, they didn't want to take the chance that they wouldn't survive and that's why they tried to escape; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That videotape that you saw today, have you ever seen that before?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. There were places, would you agree, where the army of the BiH was the aggressor during this war? I'm not talking about any of your experience but there were places where the army of the BiH was the aggressor. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, wait before you answer. Ms. Korner, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I object to that question, Your Honour. We have been over this again and again, tu quoque is not a Defence. The BiH Army may have been the aggressor somewhere else in Bosnia. It's got nothing to do with this witness or, indeed, nor do I think this witness is probably capable of answering such a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Objection sustained. If you want to rephrase the question in some other manner, Mrs. Baruch, I will allow it but --

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: I think it was engendered by the words on the video that the Court is going to ignore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's better --

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Forget it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you and your cousin were watching television, watching the news on television, when your other cousin showed up in Garici?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That is correct. I was watching news with my mom and other cousin, yeah, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what news station or where the transmission was from that you were watching?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Local news from -- that was coming from Serb side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I ask what you're studying?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Business management.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And would it be correct that the -- again going back to that mosque that we saw in the videotape, it's your understanding that that mosque had been shelled during the shelling of Vecici; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I was interested when I was reading your statement with regard to your pointing out that some Muslim villages signed loyalty oaths and gave up their arms. I'm not sure I have all of them down here, but can you tell me the ones that you remember that had done that.

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Cirkino Brdo, Nafici [phoen], Garici, Vakufci.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you were going to say?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And those villages where the people signed an oath that they were not going to take up arms against the Serbs and gave up their arms, those villages were safe for you and your mother to stay at; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Not really, because when we went to Cirkino Brdo, the first time we went to Plitska and the food ran out and no water, a guy from Cirkino Brdo, Hasin [phoen] village came over who gave a weapon or if he had it, I don't know. But we lived in his house and when the Serbs find out that he was feeding us from Hrvacani, then they told if they come back and find us they are going to kill him and kill all of us so we decided to move back to Plitska, Bilice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I guess I worded that in a way I didn't mean to. Those villages that gave up their arms and signed the loyalty oaths that they would not fight with the Serbs, those villages were safe for those people?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The thing that the Serbs didn't want them to do was to harbour people from your village, Hrvacani, because your village had not, to your knowledge, signed a loyalty oath; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: See, I mentioned they never -- I don't remember Serbs giving us an opportunity to surrender.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that you were not aware of that. You're not saying it didn't happen, you were just 14 years old at the time?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you don't know of that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't know -- I think you said that's correct.

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now your father, your father was with the fighting men, and your father was with fighting men at -- help me with the names of the places, Bilice?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: No my father went first time when I saw him he was in Bilice and that night he left for Vecici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, but when you saw him at Bilice you said I think it was a Croat place?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And a big place and there were people with lots of guns and your father was there before you even got there and --

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your father and your brother were there and your father, to your knowledge, had a gun; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, your father had left you and your mother, he didn't leave you and your mother so that he could go to a safer place; did he?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't think your father would leave you at a less safe place than he was going to; do you?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
