utterances.text: Okay. But every place that your father went with his gun, there was fighting with the Serbs; is that true, like Bilice?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: No. I never said he stayed in Bilice. He left when we were in Bilice he left that night, as he came to us and he says, I'm going to Vecici. He never was in Bilice but that day when we escaped from Hrvacani and same day, same night, he left for Vecici and that's where he stayed pretty much until we got out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But he was at Bilice when you went there, when you got there?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: But that's only one day, because we escaped that morning with shelling and for same day, you know, we got to Bilice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you have conversations with your father asking him what -- where he had been and what he had been doing while he was away from you?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have conversations with your brother, with regard to where he had been and what he had been doing while he was away from you?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sometimes I hear your voice. I hear it and I understand you, which I can't do with some witnesses, but I don't know if it's coming through. And do you know if there had been fighting at Hrvacani -- your village, Hrvacani?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Hrvacani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Hrvacani?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I don't know because I was in the basement with my mom and we were gathering together. I have no idea because there was bombing and shelling. I didn't walk out until the morning when my father came and told us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: So I don't know if fighting was going on or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So while you're in the basement in your village of Hrvacani, your father and brother were not with you?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That is correct, they were not with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did hear shelling and shooting while you were in the basement; correct?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you got to Bilice, and your father was there, you could see signs that there had been fighting there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: In Bilice?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes, because while -- I said yes, because when we walked there on the Croat army had trenches and all that so --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And of course, when you went to Vecici, there were lots of signs that there had been fighting there and your father was fighting there too; wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I don't know if he was fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But he had witness there for quite a while?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you said --

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You started out your statement talking about how you -- and I think your cousin -- would be in your village, Hrvacani, which was up higher than the other Serb villages in the area, and you would be looking through binoculars to try to figure out what was going on at those villages; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I ask you where you got your binoculars?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I got it from my father. As I mentioned before he was a hunter. He had it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. When you noticed activity in the villages around you, did you go back and, of course, tell your father, the adult of your family, what you had seen?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: As I mentioned before, hodza was taking trip around the houses, visiting houses, and that was the second day of your holiday, Bajram, and they were already in the house, they knew what was going on, so we little kids, as I was, you know, with other kids we were just watching and nothing -- but I didn't talk to him and mention anything about, you know --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that your father, as you just said, knew what was going on, but certainly, if you saw something as important as interesting and as anxiety-filling as you described what you saw, certainly you would have reported that to an adult; wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes. I did talk to my nom and we were sitting in the house when I said tanks were at Novakovo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you and your cousin would be out looking through the binoculars and then if you saw something interesting or exciting or dangerous you did report it to an adult?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes, my mom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And I'm sorry I'm jumping around, I made notes as you were talking, so I'm going in reverse order of your testimony. You were talking about the elderly people who remained in your village of Hrvacani. The first time that you left, when you say elderly, could you give me some idea? Because from my standpoint, elderly could be different from your standpoint.

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Ibro Dugonjic who was killed, when we came back and we found him burned. I would say he was approximately -- over 50 years old.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: But I don't know, I can't -- I don't know --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The other people? Okay. And the person Dugonjic - is that what his name was - that you found, that man was burnt inside his house when you found him?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And many of the houses had been burnt; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That is correct, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find any sign that people had located him before his house was burnt? Did you find any indication of that?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: No, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You said as you were leaving your village, Hrvacani, the first time, and you came to a lower area, there were snipers, there were people who were shooting, and you crawled part of the way to avoid those bullets. Do you know how many people were shooting?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I don't know but I know it was terrifying because they were shooting trees above us, all the, you know, branches and all the leaves and they were just falling down. But I don't know because two directions -- I know for a fact that fire was coming from Novakovo Brdo and Tepici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know if there was any shooting closer to Hrvacani, before you got to the dipping area? Not that you remember?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's logical that, as a young -- young man, you would remember the part where you were actually in physical danger much more strongly; would you agree?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Was there a place in your village that people would go to get information, public information; that is, someone was trying to broadcast to the village and let me give you an example. I know when I try to describe something sometimes it comes out more complicated. Sometimes in a village there is a place where posters are put up, where official notices get put. Was there a place like that in your village?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: No, ma'am. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Was there any official building in your village? I'm not talking about religious buildings, I'm talking about official buildings, like a -- I know it wasn't a municipality but a village centre, something like that?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: No, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So if somebody wanted to communicate with the men of your town or the leaders of your -- sorry, village, Hrvacani - would those leaders have to go some place else or --

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Most of the time we go to mosque if we have something, we go to mosque, especially on the Friday prayers, people gathered together and --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But at the mosque, would there be women and children there as well?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: During the Friday's prayer, no, because women and children, they are not allowed to attend Friday's praying but --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you actually in a mosque conduct official business during the prayer time?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't think so.

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Friday - this is a part of our religion - during the Friday, it's called Dzuma. Women are not allowed to be in the mosque.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, I understood that and I accept that.

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But my question was, you said you could get information at the mosque but I'm trying to establish whether or not the men of the village would conduct business during a prayer session at the mosque?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Oh, no. Normally when they have to talk about something, and if something is going on, that's after the praying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: After the prayer, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if the people from the municipality, Kotor Varos, wanted to communicate with your -- the leaders of your village, how would that go on? If you know. I know you were young at the time.

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You said at the beginning of the Bajram holidays, a lot of people gathered in your home, which was very large, and the men started talking about who has guns, and your father at that point said that your mother and you should leave the room.

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your father at -- frequently -- was it something usual for your father and a social occasion like a religious holiday, to ask you and your mother to leave the room?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I know we left the room. I don't know why. But he just told us and I respect my father so when he says, don't do it, and go or something, I do it as he said. But I don't know, I didn't want to argue with him or anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You started -- I guess my question was, was that something your father would frequently tell you to do, go out of the room?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Well, if something is important, then I'll go but normally --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Normally he didn't?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you also started out your statement talking about various attempts to contact your sister and Akif's sister. Do you know why Akif was trying to call your sister Hamida?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Because he was at that time he was in our house, and we were trying, and as a matter of fact, I tried to contact, and a lot of noises and stuff going on. So I said something is wrong with the telephone and then he asked, can I try it? So that's when he tried it and he says a lot of interference, a lot of people are talking at the same time, and he just -- we just wanted to call her and see how is she doing and what's going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And also, Akif's sister, who was living in Vrbanjci, called him. Do you know what she was calling about?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I don't know why she called him, but she called him just to tell him that two tanks were taking place in Vrbanjci and that she was having a hard time to reach him. She just wanted to talk to him, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Akif, did he live in Vrbanjci?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: No. He was -- he lived next house, next to mine. He was my neighbour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you talked about one occasion when a very heavily-armed or more than one very heavily armed Serb soldiers walked through Hrvacani?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Hrvacani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Hrvacani. I think -- I think that you said in your statement that they had a bet that nothing would happen to them if they walked through your village. Is that what you heard?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told you that?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: People when we escaped to Plitska and people were talking so --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now your brother -- let me just ask about that. As a 14 year old, why would you believe that the fact that the soldier bet, nobody in your village was going to hurt him or do anything to him, as he walked through, why would you believe that that action meant war?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't know why, but --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that's what you thought?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That's what I heard, they had a bet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And your brother, and I'm afraid -- wait a minute, I think I wrote down his name, Ahmedin?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Ahmedin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the day of the fighting in your village, your brother was actually in the military; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I think he must have told you this, because you wrote it in your statement, that he left the military and he left his military training, because people in your village were referring to him as a Chetnik?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He told you that?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The people in your village didn't distinguish between a Muslim who they knew who had grown up there, who was in the JNA, they didn't distinguish enough to know that he wasn't a Chetnik?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So I think that what you're saying is the people in the village thought if anybody was in uniform and being in the army, they were going to be Chetniks; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. The villages, Tepici and Savici, that were quite close to your village, they were actually below, because your village was the highest on the hill; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Tepici was north of Hrvacani and they were on the same -- I'd say low -- on the same level but Savici, they were a little lower and Novakovo Brdo too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you got concerned when you saw them building trenches; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you see trenches as a defensive manoeuvre or an offensive manoeuvre, Mr. Pasic?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Vrbanjci is another village that you mentioned. I think it's the one that your sister lived in or Atif's sister lived in. What was the ethnicity of that village?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, can you repeat that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I know, I got lost in the name.

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's -- you said that Akif's sister who was living in Vrbanjci, what was the ethnicity of that village?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Mainly it was a Muslim village but I know there were some Croats and Serbs too but I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about how far was it from Hrvacani?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Hrvacani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Hrvacani?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Five kilometres approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said one of the villages actually two of them, I think -- I'm sorry, Tepici and Savici were 100 per cent Serbs. Was Hrvacani 100 per cent Muslim?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm wondering if you are related to a man named Ibrahim Pasic, a history professor at Sarajevo university? Not to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: No ma'am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm come to learn by reading your statement and other documents that your name is pretty common. There are a lot of people with the name Pasic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes, maybe you mixed it up because I mentioned Ibrahim Pasic was my cousin who got killed in Vecici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I did mix it up. I was wondering if that was your cousin but then I realised your cousin had been killed. So I was just wondering, since your father actually worked in Sarajevo, before the fighting began, if maybe you also had some other relative by the name of Ibrahim Pasic who was a professor at Sarajevo university. But if you don't know that's fine?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know for sure you don't or you just don't know?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I don't know Ibrahim Pasic, a professor, I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know somebody named Sema Pasic?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about Said Pasic?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Said Pasic?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me tell you how I got that name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you want to know the relevance, Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I do, rather, particularly as it would be nice if the witness could finish today. And it seems that asking irrelevant questions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's the relevance of these questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: I have an exhibit here that I would like to offer that indicates that Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Wait. I don't know what exhibit this is. I haven't seen it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Fine, I will give it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And before anything is given to the witness I'd like to see what it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Obviously I'm not going to let the witness see it before -- but what's the relevance -- first of all, I mean forget the professor now because we have an answer about that, he doesn't know him but it's not only the professor, then it's Said Pasic and so on and what's -- what are you trying to get from the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: I'm trying to find out if he knew this person that became head of the War Presidency in Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Even so, even if he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If he did, so what?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's going to change?

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Well, I think that this is -- I think that this is pretty important and puts in context the situation in that area that there was a War Presidency and I would be more than happy to let everybody see my exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I mean, that's -- the Defence case is the time when they can put in all the evidence they want to to show what else was going on, provided its relevant, but how is this witness who was in Vecici for all of four days, and aged 14 at the time, supposed to be able to comment on any of this?

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: I'm trying to find out if he knew this person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's the name of this person?

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Said Pasic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of Said Pasic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who was appointed to the War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Don't answer that question. If you want to bring evidence about the War Presidency bring it at the right time but not through this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be correct, Mr. Pasic, that there were many people from your village who organised into military force to assist the Bosnian forces?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if I said some names, would you be in a position to know whether or not you saw them at Vecici?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Namko Turan; do you know him?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll just say the names that I know and if you know somebody let me know. Alija Mensil [phoen], Elmedin Turan, Garo [phoen] Turan, Sead Mensil, Efem Mensil, Sakib Pasic, Akif Pasic, was that one of your cousins?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Ibrahim Pasic that was your cousin as well?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: Yeah, who died.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have an exhibit here which is a statement provided by the Prosecution that --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: May I just finish telling you what I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just a moment, not in front of the witness you may not. One: The rule is that you should provide us in advance with the exhibits you intend to use.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: It's your exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Two: I have already made objections to statements by other witnesses being put in like this. It's not a proper way of leading evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What do we have there, a statement by another witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: This is an official document, apparently, listing the people who were fighting at Vecici. I've gotten it from the Prosecutor and I would like to put it in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But the procedure here is that you let us know -- not just us but the prosecuting officer also what documents you intend to make use in the course of the testimony of -- in the course of your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is the document from where you are -- has it been tendered in evidence already or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: I can't answer that, I'm sorry, because I have not been here every day. I just know I got it from the Prosecutor and it's a Banja Luka document from state security.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sure that's right. We have handed over thousands of them. Your Honour it has to be something that the witness himself can deal with. Anything else can either come in as part of the Defence case or I'm sure we will be prepared to admit it if it's relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think at this point, the position that we must take is the following: That the witness -- this is the starting point: The witness has already told you, Mrs. Baruch, that he is not aware of any such -- let's call it resistance group or whatever, in -- I go to the previous page so that I get --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, maybe I can cut this short. Can I see the document, please, that you want to put in?

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Your question before was, "Would it be correct, Mr. Pasic that there were many people from your village who organised into military force to assist the Bosnian forces?" And he answered, "I don't know." So you might as well tender into exhibit -- into evidence a list which purportedly shows who was organised in a military force.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour this is one of the so-called official notes or statements taken by the Serbs and it's -- I object to its admission in this form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: It's not yours?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's not one of yours. It's a document that was in the Banja Luka CSB but it's actually -- it purports to be a statement taken under whatever circumstances from someone which gives a list of names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If it's a statement by someone, by someone else, no. I mean, and I think he's already answered you. He told you he's not aware of any such military force. So for all intents and purposes, if you want to make use of it at some later point in time, yes, by all means.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Okay but I am confused about one thing since Ms. Korner said that the only thing that can be offered is something about which the witness himself was aware, then I didn't learn that lesson because I see the Prosecutors do it over and over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's not go into this. Please, do you have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Not many, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's already quarter to 2 and we can't keep anyone here waiting and I don't like this because you should have made an effort to finish with this witness now, this morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: If you just give me a second. I think I am finished if you just give me a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. My apologies to the interpreters and technicians and everyone but we will soon finish.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Yes, I only have two little areas, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first was, when you were at Bilice, you saw not only your father who you told this Court was just there for one day, although you hadn't questioned him about where he had been but you also saw your brother and your cousins, Nihad Mehmedalija, Sakib, Ibrahim, Mustafa and your uncle Safik, and your neighbours Redzo Pasic and his sons and your neighbour Alija and his brothers, Refik, Alija and Fazil, all there at Bilice; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see all of those people with guns?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did all of those people go in the direction of Vecici?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: I have no idea, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The second thing is you talked about somebody telling you in Vecici that some people were killed at the hospital. The people who you were told were in the hospital, those people had been fighters, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That's not true, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know if they were fighters?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: No, I have no idea if they were fighters or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would it also be correct that you have no idea what was going on immediately before they were killed? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELVEDIN PASIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Okay. Those are my only questions. I pass the witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Baruch. Thank you, Mr. Pasic. And thank you on behalf of myself -- is there -- I don't think there is any re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I would have stood up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I apologise to you, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We also had some questions to put but I don't think we can keep anyone here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it's fair to say he's almost certainly here tomorrow. If Your Honours do have questions you would like to put. He will shall here tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. I think the witness has been here long enough. Mr. Pasic, on behalf of my own behalf and on behalf of Judge Janu and Judge Taya and on behalf of the Tribunal generally, I should like to thank you for having come over to give testimony which must have been difficult for you. I realise that. You will receive all the assistance you require to enable you to return to your country at the earliest possible opportunity, occasion. And may I on behalf of everyone wish you a safe journey back home, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Tomorrow we start with BT95.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, start and go on I think with BT95.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The day after too.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The day after and if necessary into Friday. Your Honour, can I put it this way, make it absolutely clear now, he's another one of those witnesses who will not be proofed. He's a witness that we say is capable of telling the truth about somethings and undoubtedly Mr. Ackerman, if he's cross-examining, will want Your Honour to warn him about the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I got you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I want to make that absolutely clear. Your Honour, I'm proposing to put in the transcript of the interview as an exhibit but I need to go through the areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I still have to read whatever we have because I haven't read anything as yet so --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will get you copies of the interview, if you have not got it already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I haven't received anything. This is what I'm saying, I have not read anything as yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right, Your Honour we will make sure you get copies of the interview this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Do we have them? May I just inquire, do we have them?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, you do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's only -- I'm speaking for myself because I have not consulted my two colleagues as yet.
